claims.text: The starting CoCrFeNi alloy is homogeneous and contains no pre-existing lubricious phases.
Yttrium can be introduced into an HEA during melt or powder processing.
Adding 1–2 wt.% yttrium to CoCrFeNi will produce a uniform yttrium distribution while avoiding brittle phases.
Adding 1–2 wt.% yttrium will promote in-situ formation of a continuous, uniform, nanoscale Y2O3 tribofilm during sliding.
During sliding, yttrium will segregate to the CoCrFeNi surface.
Surface-segregated yttrium will oxidize in situ to form Y2O3.
The resulting Y2O3 tribofilm will remain adherent and stable from room temperature to 800 °C.
The Y2O3 tribofilm has sufficiently low shear strength to act as a lubricious layer.
The Y2O3 tribofilm has high thermal stability over the proposed test range.
The Y2O3 tribofilm will reduce direct metal-to-metal contact.
Reduced metal-to-metal contact will lower friction and wear at elevated temperatures and under variable loading.
Relative to undoped CoCrFeNi, the yttrium-modified alloy will have lower and more stable friction coefficients at every tested temperature from room temperature to 800 °C.
Relative to undoped CoCrFeNi, the yttrium-modified alloy will have lower wear rates at every tested temperature from room temperature to 800 °C.
Untreated CoCrFeNi tends to exhibit increased friction and wear at higher temperatures because its natural lubricity breaks down under severe conditions.
Yttrium contents below the proposed 1–2 wt.% range may be insufficient to form the required tribofilm.
Yttrium contents above the proposed 1–2 wt.% range may cause deleterious brittle-phase formation.
The proposed benefit applies in ambient air under high and variable loads from room temperature to 800 °C.
Failure to achieve more than 15% reductions in both friction coefficient and wear rate across the full temperature range, or failure to observe a uniform Y2O3 layer, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis claims effectiveness under varying environmental conditions, whereas the specified test conditions and boundary are limited to ambient air. No non-ambient environments or environmental limits are defined.
